question: Switch to database concurrency: your overlap constructions preserved all counts; now test whether transactions preserve an invariant. PostgreSQL has two doctor rows, Alice and Bob, both marked on call. At repeatable-read isolation, each transaction counts on-call doctors and, if the count exceeds one, marks its own doctor off call. Alice and Bob run concurrently. Show an exact interleaving where both commit and nobody remains on call. Why does updating different rows matter? [Interviewer pause: one point five seconds.] Provide executable SQL using serializable isolation that preserves at least one on-call doctor, specify exactly what must be retried after a serialization failure, and justify correctness.

I’m interpreting “uncall” as “on-call.” REPEATABLE READ permits write skew here; SERIALIZABLE preserves the invariant if every relevant writer follows the protocol and retries the whole transaction after a serialization failure.

An exact repeatable-read execution is:
1. Alice begins and counts 2 on-call doctors; 2 > 1 is true.
2. Bob begins and counts 2 before either update; his condition is also true.
3. Alice updates her own row to off call. Her snapshot still shows Bob on call.
4. Bob updates his own row to off call. His snapshot still shows Alice on call.
5. Alice commits, then Bob commits. The final count is zero.
